comments.body:
Related diagnostic requirement from recent warning/assertion location work:

Diagnostic file context must point to user configuration definitions, not the Home Manager module that emitted the diagnostic.

`config.warnings` is a plain list of strings, so generic enrichment via `options.warnings.definitionsWithLocations` only finds where the warning was added to `warnings`. For module-generated warnings this often points at `modules/...`, which is not actionable for users.

Better direction:

- deprecation helpers should accept `options` + `option` path and derive `files = options.<path>.files`
- non-deprecation warnings should use a helper like `lib.hm.diagnostics.warningForOption`
- assertions should carry `relatedOptions`, and assertion formatting can derive files from those option definitions
- avoid global warning enrichment unless warnings become structured values

This fits the broader helper-consolidation goal: central helpers should make actionable diagnostics cheap, while preserving user-owned definition locations.
It would be good to consider a helper as well for modular services or what will eventually become package modules.

issue.body:
### Module Name

`lib.hm` / module infrastructure

### Requested Feature

Add opt-in helper APIs for module shapes that Home Manager already repeats
across many modules:

- `lib.hm.modules.mkProgramModule`: factory for simple program modules with
  `enable`, nullable `package`, typed freeform `settings`, package
  installation, and config-file generation.
- `lib.hm.services` helpers: shared service wiring for common systemd/launchd
  patterns, graphical-session units, and generated config restart triggers.
- `lib.hm.darwin` config path helper: one place for choosing Linux XDG paths
  vs macOS `Library/Application Support` / `Library/Preferences` paths.

Goal is not mass abstraction. Goal is to capture conventions already used in
tree, make new modules cheaper to review, and reduce drift when same option
shape or service wiring appears repeatedly.

Proposed follow-up issues:

- [ ] #9472 `lib.hm.modules.mkProgramModule`
- [ ] #9473 `lib.hm.services` helpers
- [ ] #9474 `lib.hm.darwin` config-path helper

### Current Limitations

Common module structure is reimplemented by hand:

- Current tree has 399 importable entries under `modules/programs` and 174
  under `modules/services`.
- Local grep survey found 102 obvious program modules with same core shape:
  `mkEnableOption`, nullable `mkPackageOption`, `settings`, `home.packages`,
  and `xdg.configFile`.
- 19 modules define both `systemd.user.services` and `launchd.agents`, often
  deriving both from same command and environment.
- 60 module files set `PartOf = [ "graphical-session.target" ]`, 46 set
  `After = [ "graphical-session.target" ]`, and 72 set
  `WantedBy = [ "graphical-session.target" ]` (file counts for the exact
  single-element pattern under `modules/`; looser patterns find more).
- 26 program/service modules define `X-Restart-Triggers`; many are coupled to
  generated config files by convention only.
- 56 module files reference `Library/Application Support` or
  `Library/Preferences` directly.

Consequences:

- New simple modules copy 25-50 lines from nearby modules.
- Small conventions drift, especially nullable package guards,
  empty-settings guards, restart triggers, and Darwin path handling.
- Reviews spend time re-checking repeated plumbing instead of module-specific
  behavior.
- Later settings additions can miss restart triggers because file generation
  and service restart wiring are separate manual edits.

### Additional Context

Existing in-tree precedent:

- `lib.hm.shell.mk*IntegrationOption` is already used heavily for shell
  integration options.
- `modules/programs/vscode/mkVscodeModule.nix` generates multiple related
  program modules from one factory.
- `modules/services-modular` already maps abstract service definitions to
  Home Manager systemd units and config files. New service helpers should be
  compatible with that direction rather than competing with it.

Ground rules:

- Helpers are opt-in.
- Migration should happen in small mechanical batches.
- Migrated modules should have zero diff in rendered option docs and generated
  files.
- Modules that no longer fit simple shapes stay hand-written.
- Helpers must preserve useful option declaration locations in generated docs.
- Service helpers must expose per-platform overrides; systemd and launchd do
  not have 1:1 semantics.

Related upstream issues found while searching:

- #3703: some service modules do not expose a `systemdTarget` option
- #5506: `swayosd` should expose `systemdTarget`
- #8034: systemd user services sometimes start without expected environment

No direct duplicate found for shared module factories/helpers.


### Prior art: nixvim

[nixvim](https://github.com/nix-community/nixvim) already runs this model at
scale. Nearly all of its plugin modules are generated by two factories,
`mkNeovimPlugin` and `mkVimPlugin`
([`lib/plugins/`](https://github.com/nix-community/nixvim/tree/main/lib/plugins)):
416 of 452 `plugins/by-name` entries (~92%) use one of them, with hand-written
modules reserved for unusual cases.

Relevant takeaways for Home Manager:

- The factory owns the repeated shape (`enable`, package resolution, typed
  freeform `settings` via a shared `mkSettingsOption`, maintainers) while
  escape hatches (`extraOptions`, `extraConfig = cfg: { ... }`, `imports`)
  absorb per-module variation. Same escape-hatch set proposed here; nixvim's
  adoption rate suggests it is sufficient in practice.
- The factory also centralizes deprecation plumbing
  (`optionsRenamedToSettings`, `deprecateExtraOptions`), so option migrations
  stay mechanical and consistent across hundreds of modules.
- Options declared through the factories render correctly in nixvim's
  generated docs, which is the same docs/declaration-location requirement
  called out above.
issue.title: [Feature Request] Add shared helpers for common module boilerplate
